questions.q: What does Automated ML do for you in Azure Machine Learning?
options: It collects the labels for your data
It tries many combinations of featurization, algorithm and hyperparameters and ranks the resulting models
It guarantees the best possible model for any problem
It replaces the need to choose a target column
questions.explain: AutoML iterates over features, algorithms and parameters and produces a leaderboard by your primary metric. You still supply the data, target and metric, and you still validate the result.

questions.q: In our local five-model comparison, plain logistic regression had the best cross-validated AUC. What is the sensible takeaway?
options: Systematic comparison can show that the simplest model is good enough or better on your data
questions.explain: The result was specific to this illustrative dataset. The point is that comparing candidates cheaply beats assuming the fanciest algorithm wins.

questions.q: In SDK v2, how is training data supplied to an AutoML tabular job?
options: As a screenshot of the table
As an MLTable input that includes the target column
questions.explain: Microsoft's guide says to upload the data through an MLTable, which must be tabular and contain the target column, and to pass it as training_data.

questions.q: Your churn data is imbalanced (about 27 percent churners). According to Microsoft's guidance, which primary metric can be a better choice than accuracy?
questions.explain: The docs note that threshold-dependent metrics like accuracy may not optimize well on small or class-skewed datasets, where AUC_weighted can be a better choice. The regression metrics do not apply to classification.

questions.q: In the studio, where do you find the models an AutoML job has produced, ordered by metric score?
options: The Models + child jobs tab of the job
questions.explain: Microsoft's studio guide says the Models + child jobs tab lists the models created, ordered by the metric score with the highest at the top by default.
